title: A Mammal That Bites Like a Snake Outlived the Dinosaurs

scenes.text: This furry animal bites like a venomous snake.
Meet the solenodon of Hispaniola. About the size of a big rat, with a long, bendy snout it pokes into cracks to find insects.
Its lower front teeth are grooved. Venomous saliva runs down the grooves straight into whatever it bites, the way a snake's fangs work.
In lab tests, the venom killed mice within minutes. No other living mammal injects venom through its teeth like this.
Its family line split from every other mammal around 76 million years ago. Dinosaurs were still walking the Earth.
The asteroid came. The dinosaurs went. The solenodon is still here, still biting.

description:
The solenodon of Hispaniola is one of the only mammals that injects venom like a snake: venomous saliva runs through grooves in its lower incisors into its prey.
Genetic studies place the split between its lineage and all other living mammals at roughly 73 to 78 million years ago, before the asteroid that ended the dinosaurs.
Which other living fossil should we cover next?

first_comment: Only a handful of mammals are venomous: the platypus, a few shrews, the slow loris and the solenodon. Which one surprised you most?
